column3: Indian rosewood (Dalbergia latifolia) clear wood, green-to-ovendry dimensional change
column4: FPL-GTR-282 Chapter 4, Table 4-4, Rosewood, Indian (Dalbergia latifolia), p. 4-9 and footnotes a-b; https://research.fs.usda.gov/download/treesearch/62243.pdf
column5: Independent radial, tangential and volumetric values in percent of green dimensions or volume. The source explicitly warns these imported-wood values were collected from world literature and may not represent a true species average. Their 0-30 percent moisture applicability is for Equation (4-9), not measurements at every moisture. Uncertainty is Unstated; no covariance, longitudinal shrinkage, graded-lumber qualification or temperature dependence is supplied.

column3: Indian rosewood clear wood at prescribed uniform dry-basis moisture
column5: Fiber saturation of 30 percent is the source-authorized approximation when unknown, not a species measurement. S(M)=S0*(1-M/0.30) uses fractions below fiber saturation for a sufficiently small piece without significant moisture gradients. Green-volume specific gravity alone remains insufficient for density at 12 percent moisture; the separate density reference combines it with independent volumetric shrinkage. No drying rate, moisture transport or thermal-density law is supplied.

column3: Indian rosewood modeled density at exactly 12 percent dry-basis moisture
column4: FPL-GTR-282 Chapter 5, Table 5-5a, existing green-volume specific gravity; Chapter 4, Table 4-4 and Equations (4-9), (4-11), (4-14), pp. 4-9 to 4-12; https://research.fs.usda.gov/download/treesearch/62243.pdf
column5: Engineering reference, not a new density measurement. The original Ggreen=0.75 is ovendry mass over green volume, so multiplying it directly by 1120 is not a 12-percent density. With separately tabulated volumetric shrinkage Sv=0.085 and explicitly approximate MCfs=0.30, V12/Vgreen=1-Sv*(1-0.12/0.30)=0.949 and rho12=1000*Ggreen*1.12/0.949=885.1422550052687 kg/m3. This combines independent literature averages without asserting a common specimen or covariance. The reference is restricted to 12 percent moisture and unknown test temperature; no conductivity or temperature-dependent density is inferred.

column3: Indian rosewood (Dalbergia latifolia) clear straight-grained specimens
column4: FPL-GTR-282 chapter 5 tabulated averages (static bending MOE; compression-derived elastic ratios; experimentally determined Poisson ratios)
column5: Average clear straight-grained small-specimen values at approximately 12 percent moisture content; the elastic-ratio and Poisson tables derive from samples of a few species and the source warns values vary within and between species; the source reports representative coefficients of variation separately in its Table 5-6 without per-value confidence metadata, so runtime uncertainty stays Unstated; bending MOE is printed with span-to-depth 14 shear deflection included and the chapter states it may be increased by 10 percent to remove that effect, which is how the derived young_modulus_longitudinal row is computed; axis convention: L longitudinal (grain), R radial, T tangential, matching the instrument-axis-convention file in this directory; Table 5-5a specific gravity is ovendry-weight over green-volume basis, so no 12-percent density is derived for this species

column3: Indian rosewood clear wood at fixed 12 percent dry-basis moisture content
column5: Species-independent engineering heat-capacity correlation, not an additional species measurement. Cp in J/(kg K) is 1000*((0.1031+0.003867*T+4.18*0.12)/1.12+12*(-0.06191+0.000236*T-0.000133*12)); its fixed-moisture dependence is affine in absolute T over 280-420 K, so linear interpolation reproduces this model. The existing specific gravity uses green volume, not the required 12-percent volume; no density or conductivity is inferred from it. No drying, phase change, pressure dependence, or graded-lumber qualification is supplied.
